title: Smug Kaomoji (￣ー￣): Copy & Paste Smirking Text Faces
meta_description: Copy and paste smug kaomoji: smug grins like (￣ー￣) and (￣︶￣), smirks (¬‿¬), Lenny faces ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°) and scheming, mischievous faces like ψ(｀∇´)ψ and (≖‿≖).
hero_tagline: Half-closed eyes and lopsided smiles for winning an argument, being right, or planning something. Each face copies with one click.
intro: Smugness in a kaomoji lives in the eyes. Flat ￣ eyes look half-closed and pleased with themselves, ¬ draws a sideways glance, and ≖ narrows the eyes into a squint that reads as scheming. The mouth stays small and closed: ー is a satisfied line, ‿ a slight curve. The Lenny face ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°) is the internet's best-known smirk, built from combining marks that float over the letters, so on some fonts the brows sit slightly off. For the 😏 picture rather than a text face, see the smirk emoji page linked below.

faq.q: What is the smug face called in text?
faq.a: The best known is the Lenny face, ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°), which spread on internet forums around 2012 and picked up the name Lenny there. Japanese-style smug faces like (￣ー￣) are simpler and use the flat ￣ eyes common in kaomoji.

faq.q: What is the difference between smug and smirk kaomoji?
faq.a: Smug faces look pleased with themselves, usually with flat eyes looking forward. Smirk faces add a sideways glance with ¬ or →, so the satisfaction is aimed at someone else.

faq.q: Why does the Lenny face look broken on some devices?
faq.a: Its brows and nose are combining marks, characters that attach to the letter before them. Fonts place them differently, so the brows can sit too high or drift sideways. Faces like (¬‿¬) avoid combining marks and look the same everywhere.
